args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api began failing health checks after the v2.3.1 deploy (unhealthy in all regions, error rate ~18%). v2.3.1-rc had also been unhealthy in staging. Rolled back all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. The first rollback attempt halted after us-east due to an orchestrator error, leaving the regions on mixed versions. A retry finished the rollout. After the rollback, all regions are on v2.3.0, the service reports healthy, and the error rate is ~0.2%. Follow-ups: root-cause the v2.3.1 failure, investigate the orchestrator partial-failure, and review why v2.3.1 was promoted despite failing in staging.

trace.error_message: Request to create_incident timed out after 30000ms

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and the SEV2 incident is open as INC-0001.

**Rollback**
- The bad release was v2.3.1. It was unhealthy in all three regions, with an error rate of about 18%. Its staging candidate (v2.3.1-rc) had also failed health checks.
- v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production, so that's the version I rolled back to.
- The first attempt stopped after us-east because of an error in the deployment system, which left the regions on different versions. I ran the same rollback again and it finished.
- us-east, us-west and eu-west are all on v2.3.0 now. The service reports healthy and the error rate is down to about 0.2%.

**Incident**
- The request to open the incident timed out. Before trying again, I checked the incident list: it had been created, so I didn't send a second request and page the on-call engineer twice.
- It's a SEV2 for checkout-api, and the summary covers what broke, the rollback, and the version mismatch partway through.
- It lists three follow-ups:
  - Find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure.
  - Look into why the deployment system stopped partway through the rollback.
  - Review why v2.3.1 went to production even though it failed in staging.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
The rollback stopped partway: us-east is on v2.3.0, but us-west and eu-west are still on v2.3.1. Rolling back to the same version is safe to repeat, so I'll retry once.
